newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call sharply higher on funds outflow fears.
newsitem.headline: Indian call sharply higher on funds outflow fears.

text.p: Fears of substantial fund outflows toward a loan issue pushed call rates up to 7.5-8.5 percent on Friday from Wednesday's close of 4.0-4.5 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said there were stray quotes by lenders up to 10.0 percent in early trade.
The call money market was inactive on Thursday as banks in the commercial capital of Bombay and most other centres were closed for a holiday.
Dealers said uncertainty over the bids received and accepted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at a loan issue on Wednesday had pushed call money rates up.
The RBI sold state government bonds worth 25 billion rupees on April 30 and results of the auction were not yet available.
"Market players expect substantial oversubscription to the issue and they also expect the RBI to retain a good part or all of the excess bids," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
"As no details are as yet available on bids received or retained, lenders are using the opportunity to drive rates up," the dealer said.
Dealers said the higher rates were lender-driven but borrowers were still quoting lower rates.
"Deals have been done up to 8.5 percent but it is fairly thin trade," said a dealer. "I think once the loan results are out, we will see rates coming down."
